name: Napalm
description: Napalm (Whipsaw/3-5-7) is a multi-stage poker variant emphasizing bluffing. 4-7 players. 52-card deck. Three stages: Stage 1 (2 cards, best high), Stage 2 (+3 community, best LOW 5-card), Stage 3 (+2 more, best HIGH 5-card). Each stage: declare 'yes/no' if you think you have best hand. Single yes=token. Multiple yes=side bets. First to collect 5 tokens wins the pot.

history.origins: This unusual poker variant was contributed by Michael Sanderson. Exact origin is unclear but it likely originated in the Northeastern USA; it was certainly played at Brandeis University (Massachusetts) and now has a following in the Maryland-Virginia area and Annapolis, where it is standard fare at several poker games. The name Napalm is of unknown origin.
timeline: 1970s–1980s: Played at Brandeis University (Massachusetts); reported as Whipsaw (1979); spread to Maryland–Virginia and Annapolis area.

setup.deck: 52 cards. Aces high. Tokens (non-monetary) + chips for side bets.

rules.objective: Be the first to collect five tokens to win the pot; players also compete in side bets matching the pot amount each time multiple players declare yes.
rules.gameplay: Ante. Stage 1: 2 cards, declare yes/no (best high 2-card). Stage 2: 3 community cards, yes/no (best LOW 5-card). Stage 3: 2 more hole cards, yes/no (best HIGH 5-card of 7). Single yes=1 token. Multiple yes=show hands, loser pays pot-sized side bet to winner.

scoring.description: Tokens: first to 5 wins pot. Side bets equal pot size.
scoring.winCondition: Collect 5 tokens to win the pot.
